title: Scaling Applications
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of scaling applications in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to processes and workers.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers scaling applications within deployment and production readiness. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use scaling applications to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is a small, well-defined behavior with explicit assumptions, a predictable result and a testable edge case.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Scaling Applications matters because it is part of deployment and production readiness. In practice, focus on a small, well-defined behavior with explicit assumptions, a predictable result and a testable edge case. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Processes and workers
items.text: Use processes and workers as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: Database connection limits
items.text: Apply database connection limits against a disposable database and synthetic data first. Make transaction ownership and cleanup explicit, parameterize values, and verify constraints and behavior after failures before considering a deployment.

items.title: Scaling WebSocket applications
items.text: For scaling websocket applications, identify which operation waits on I/O, which resources remain open, and what happens on timeout or disconnect. Async syntax does not make CPU-bound work faster or durable background jobs reliable by itself.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Scaling Applications
content_blocks.code:
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text

engine = create_engine("sqlite:///./lab.db")
with engine.begin() as connection:
    result = connection.execute(text("SELECT 1 AS ok"))
    print(result.scalar_one())
content_blocks.run_instructions: This tiny SQLAlchemy connection smoke test uses local SQLite. Use parameterized statements for values; place real credentials in environment configuration.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.
content_blocks.limitations: This code is inspectable lesson material, not executed by CodeLeaf. Run it only in a local virtual environment or a separately isolated runner with resource/time/network limits. Security examples are sketches, not complete production authentication or authorization systems.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “Processes and workers”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Scaling Applications”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Processes and workers” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Scaling Applications, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.

summary: Scaling Applications belongs to the broader goal of a small, well-defined behavior with explicit assumptions, a predictable result and a testable edge case.
Use the source subtopics as the completeness checklist and verify expected results rather than relying on intuition.
Examples in this course are illustrative until technically reviewed and executed on a supported local environment.
